appraisal_events.evidence: il jeta en souriant à M. de Charlus un regard niaisement interrogateur et concupiscent ; 'Mais voyons, bien entendu', dit M. de Charlus, de l'air docte d'un érudit parlant à un ignare ; M. de Vaugoubert ne détacha plus ses yeux de ces jeunes secrétaires (ce qui agaça beaucoup M. de Charlus).
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator frames Vaugoubert's eager, foolish stare and Charlus's condescending, expert-to-novice tone as a comparison that leaves Vaugoubert looking clumsy and avid, while Charlus is positioned as the knowing authority he annoys.

status_effects.explanation: Vaugoubert is shown as foolishly avid ('niaisement interrogateur et concupiscent') and unable to hide his crude curiosity, which the narrator treats unflatteringly.
Charlus speaks with the assured, doctoral tone of an expert instructing an ignoramus, locally elevating his authority relative to Vaugoubert even as Vaugoubert's continued staring irritates him.
